sections.html:
The Yadkin County Register of Deeds in Yadkinville keeps the county's land records: deeds, deeds of trust, maps and related filings. Those records are open to public inspection. Staff also copy and certify birth, death and marriage certificates, issue marriage licenses and swear in notaries.

A sale is only fully protected once the deed is on the books. An unregistered conveyance loses to lien creditors and later buyers who paid value, and whoever registers first generally ranks first (G.S. 47-18).

The county encourages electronic recording for every document. Marriage licenses and notary oaths run by appointment through 336-849-7904. The register of deeds is an elected post, and the excise tax on deeds is collected at this same counter.

sections.h2: How a deed gets recorded after a sale
sections.html:
Usually the attorney or title company at the closing table sends it electronically. The register accepts every document type except maps by e-recording. A firm that wants to submit must go through Simplifile, CSC or ePN and complete a submitter agreement that the provider passes to the county.

For deed work, the Yadkin County tax office tells owners to consult an attorney. Sellers in Yadkinville, Jonesville, East Bend or on a rural road in between therefore rarely deal with the recording desk themselves.

  • Ask whether your closing firm already has an e-recording agreement with Yadkin County.
  • Find out who is writing the check for the excise tax, since the statute assigns it to the seller.
  • Keep the recording confirmation as proof of the date and time of registration.
  • Bringing paper instead? Phone the office before you drive over.

One statewide schedule applies here. It is complete and exclusive, and payment is due up front (G.S. 161-10).

Register of Deeds charges that touch a house sale

Count the pages in your deed and exhibits before closing, because the $4.00 charge starts on the sixteenth page of a general instrument.

The person transferring the house pays it. The rate is one dollar per five hundred dollars of value, due at the register's counter ahead of the filing (G.S. 105-228.30).

Collections are divided evenly. Half stays with the county. The other half goes to the state monthly, and the county may retain 2 percent of it. Your closing statement lists the dollar figure that applies to your price.

If a house passes as a gift or between relatives, ask the office how a stated value is treated before anyone signs.

sections.h2: Tax office versus Register of Deeds
sections.html:
They are separate counters. The Yadkin County Tax Department in Yadkinville lists and bills property, takes exemption applications and keeps the parcel maps. The register of deeds only records the paper. A 2027 revaluation is underway at the tax office.

For billing and payment questions, call the tax office at 336-849-7903. It offers an August discount of 2 percent, plus a solid waste fee of $76.00 per household, or $38.00 with the elderly exemption. Taxes fall due September 1, and interest starts January 6.

More than deeds. Options, leases beyond three years and rights of first refusal must be registered before they bind a later buyer. A seller who gave a buyer an option months ago should check that it was recorded, since an unrecorded one may not hold up against a new purchaser.

A seller-financed sale is the other case worth knowing. North Carolina's Chapter 47H covers a contract for deed with five or more payments, where the seller keeps title. Written and acknowledged terms are required, the buyer gets a three-business-day cancellation window, and the seller records the contract or a memorandum within five business days. A forfeiture notice has to allow at least 30 days to cure (Chapter 47H).

  • Satisfactions of a deed of trust record for no fee, so paying off a mortgage costs nothing at this office.
  • For a parcel split between counties, the excise tax goes to the county holding the greater value.
  • An estate sale may require a small estate affidavit to list each tract the decedent owned.

sections.h2: Sales of inherited and older houses
sections.html:
Yadkin County has 17,697 housing units and owners live in 76.9 percent of them, so many sales involve inherited or older houses. New construction is slow, with 116 building permits in 2025.

For an estate, the clerk of superior court can say who has authority to sign the deed. The register of deeds will record it once it is signed and acknowledged, but staff cannot tell you whether the signer has that authority.

sections.h2: If the owner has a tax lien
sections.html:
An owner facing a tax lien can look at the county's Tax Foreclosure Sales page to see how auctions are listed. Redemption remains possible before a sale is confirmed.

A buyer's title examiner will find any lien, so clear it before listing. Ask the tax office for a payoff figure that includes the solid waste fee, and give it to the closing attorney.

1. Confirm with your attorney how the deed will be recorded, electronically or on paper.
  2. Count the pages in the deed and exhibits to estimate the recording fee.
  3. Find out who will write the check for the excise tax.
  4. Check that any old mortgage has a recorded satisfaction.
  5. Keep the recording confirmation with your closing papers.

A cash sale skips the buyer's lender and its deed of trust, so the packet is smaller, but the deed and the excise tax are still recorded in the same way.

faqs.q: Does Yadkin County charge a transfer tax on a sale?
faqs.a: Yes. The seller owes a deed excise tax, paid to the register at filing. The rate is one dollar for each five hundred dollars of value.

faqs.q: Can a Yadkin County deed be recorded electronically?
faqs.a: Yes, any document except a map. The attorney or title company must first sign a submitter agreement through Simplifile, CSC or ePN. For paper filings, phone 336-849-7904.

faqs.q: Does it cost anything to record a satisfaction of a mortgage?
faqs.a: No. State law sets no charge for a satisfaction, so the payoff paperwork is free to file.

faqs.q: How long does a buyer under a contract for deed have to cancel?
faqs.a: Through midnight of the third business day. After that, the seller has a five-business-day window to record.

faqs.q: Is a Yadkin County revaluation coming?
faqs.a: Yes, a 2027 revaluation is underway. Counties must reappraise all real estate on an eight-year cycle at the longest.
